_note: For the Radiation Passport. Numbers below are from the cited sources. Where sources disagree the conflict is flagged. Agent: show only items with status 'ok' as exact; show others as 'about'.

comparisons.label: A year of normal radiation on Earth (average)
comparisons.source: NASA via ABC News 2024 says about 2 mSv. NASA NTRS 20090026571 uses 3.6 mSv for the US average. Show 'about 2 to 4 mSv'.

comparisons.label: Six months on the ISS
comparisons.source: NASA 2017 report as cited by ABC News and STCE. Lower end at solar maximum, higher at solar minimum.

comparisons.label: One day on the ISS
comparisons.source: Derived: 80-160 mSv divided by about 182 days. Mark as 'about'.

conflicts: ABC News says NASA equates 1 mSv to about 3 chest X-rays. STCE says about 10. With 0.1 mSv per chest X-ray (NASA NTRS), 1 mSv is 10 X-rays. Use the NTRS number and compute.
NTRS slide says 'one day in space is about 2.5 chest X-rays'. That does not match 80-160 mSv per six months. Do not use it.
game: In-game dose is in 'game units' from 0 to 100, scaled for kids. Always say so on screen.
